drvprog.evidence: holdout ranging separation -0.319 (p=0.020) but +0.160 in 2016-19, the WRONG SIGN, turning negative only from 2020. A post-COVID rate-cycle artefact.

drvprog.good_for: confirming the CURRENT regime, crisis especially
drvprog.decided_by: separation -- held sign in every sub-period
drvprog.evidence: crisis days read ~0.9 sd above everything else; range-leaning -0.538 / -0.314 / -0.648 across the three holdout sub-periods, same sign and size throughout. Holdout null p=0.020.

crisis separation +0.172 in-sample (p=0.020) flips to -0.071 on the holdout (p=0.647); sub-periods +0.112 / -0.105 / -0.139. Mechanism check technically held (JPY/CHF |sep| 0.238 vs 0.199) but the largest single pair was EURAUD, not a funding cross.

drvprog.decided_by: separation -- sign flip between halves AND sub-periods
drvprog.evidence: crisis separation -0.108 in-sample flips to +0.082 on the holdout; sub-periods +0.073 / -0.650 / +0.224. Fails both nulls (p=0.569, p=0.686). Only 10 of 28 pairs testable: AUD and CAD have a 2y but no daily 10y, NZD has neither.

trending separation -0.199 in-sample (p=0.039) holds sign on the holdout (-0.107) but fails its null there (p=0.431), and sub-periods flip: -0.122 / -0.532 / +0.150. Forward crisis lift was x1.17 in BOTH halves -- the most consistent forward number in the programme -- but fails its null in both (p=0.255, p=0.235).

drvprog.decided_by: separation -- sign flips on every reading
drvprog.evidence: All four readings flip. |4-week change| is the sharpest: ranging +0.246 in-sample (p=0.020) reverses to -0.193 on the holdout (p=0.078) -- beats its null in BOTH halves with OPPOSITE signs, which is a real magnitude attached to an unreliable sign. The declared crowded-trade cell (top decile |net| vs P(acute crisis in 20 bars)) held direction, x1.32 in-sample and x1.21 on the holdout, but fails its null in both (p=0.196, p=0.412) -- the same shape as commodities. Reaches 7 of 28 pairs, no crosses; NZD ends 2022-02-01.
Dairy (GDT auction) and coal are not free. Iron ore TIO=F IS free but only from 2010-10-14 and is scoped to AUD, which gold already covers. Recorded as untestable rather than tested badly.

pairmech.mechanism: USDJPY: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while JPY strengthens when global risk rises and carry trades unwind, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 1 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

AUDJPY: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 2 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

GBPUSD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while GBP moves on UK policy and its own politics, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 3 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

EURJPY: A haven leg against a large, slow bloc, so risk-off episodes move it in one direction for weeks at a time. It sits at rank 4 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

EURUSD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while EUR moves on ECB policy and growth differentials, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 5 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

CADJPY: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 6 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

NZDJPY: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 7 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

AUDCAD: Two currencies driven by the same global demand cycle, so much of the move cancels and what is left is range-bound. It sits at rank 8 of 28 on trendiness, so it is one of the more directional pairs in the set.

NZDUSD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while NZD moves on soft commodities and global risk appetite, with the thinnest liquidity of the eight, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 9 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

AUDNZD: Two currencies driven by the same global demand cycle, so much of the move cancels and what is left is range-bound. It sits at rank 10 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

CHFJPY: Both are bid when risk rises, so they largely offset and the pair moves on the difference between two central banks. It sits at rank 11 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

NZDCAD: Two currencies driven by the same global demand cycle, so much of the move cancels and what is left is range-bound. It sits at rank 12 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

EURCHF: A haven leg against a large, slow bloc, so risk-off episodes move it in one direction for weeks at a time. It sits at rank 13 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

AUDCHF: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 14 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

AUDUSD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while AUD moves on industrial demand and global risk appetite, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 15 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

EURAUD: A large, slow bloc against a commodity and China-growth proxy, so it moves on the gap between two policy cycles. It sits at rank 16 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

EURNZD: A large, slow bloc against a small commodity currency, so it moves on the gap between two policy cycles. It sits at rank 17 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

GBPJPY: A haven leg against a mid-sized open economy, so risk-off episodes move it in one direction for weeks at a time. It sits at rank 18 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

GBPAUD: A mid-sized open economy against a commodity and China-growth proxy, so it moves on the gap between two policy cycles. It sits at rank 19 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

NZDCHF: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 20 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

USDCAD: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while CAD moves on crude and on the US economy it borders, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 21 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

USDCHF: The dollar leg carries global risk and rates while CHF strengthens when European risk rises, and is periodically managed by its central bank, so the pair trends when those two stories diverge and ranges when they agree. It sits at rank 22 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

EURCAD: A large, slow bloc against an oil-linked North American currency, so it moves on the gap between two policy cycles. It sits at rank 23 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

GBPNZD: A mid-sized open economy against a small commodity currency, so it moves on the gap between two policy cycles. It sits at rank 24 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

GBPCHF: A haven leg against a mid-sized open economy, so risk-off episodes move it in one direction for weeks at a time. It sits at rank 25 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

EURGBP: Two neighbouring economies on similar policy paths, so the two legs mostly cancel and the pair spends its time going nowhere. It sits at rank 26 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

CADCHF: One side is bid when risk rises and the other is sold, so a single shift in global risk pushes both legs the same way at once -- the cleanest trending structure in the set. It sits at rank 27 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

GBPCAD: A mid-sized open economy against an oil-linked North American currency, so it moves on the gap between two policy cycles. It sits at rank 28 of 28 on trendiness, so it spends more of its life range-bound than trending.

SNB signals it will no longer act decisively against appreciation, and the franc is bid as a haven through the euro-area sovereign crisis. Ends the day the SNB imposes the 1.20 floor.

crisis_witnesses.what: Two more witnesses beside the acute detector and MOVE. Panel turbulence is the Mahalanobis distance of the day's return vector from its own history under the trailing covariance: a day is turbulent when moves are big OR unusually combined. Roll illiquidity is the effective-spread proxy from the negative autocovariance of daily price changes, closes only.
crisis_witnesses.what_it_is_not: CONFIRMATION, NEVER PREDICTION. Both are read on the day, lagged one bar, and validated on a forward-only window from each news-dated event to +15 days that never opens before the event. Neither forecasts a crisis, neither is a state, and neither replaces the acute detector or MOVE -- a witness earns its place only by adding coverage or an independent vote.

l2_restart.note: Layer 2 restarted from mode A up (HANDOFF 0l). The gate 1 on disk cut on W2+W3 pooled = 2011-2020, i.e. on every year Layer 2 then called blind, and charged no costs. The honest gate 1 scores every combination at defaults with costs on, banks each trade by the calendar year of its ENTRY bar, and CUTS ON TUNE YEARS ONLY -- grade and trade years are measured at the same time and take no part in the selection. Four streams, none selected on: trend and chop, each routed and always-on. The cut is swept over its whole range; Jack picks from the curve. Nothing from the old Layer 2 is deleted.

contaminations.what: l2sweep.score_combo scores a combination on W2 + W3 pooled, i.e. 2011-01-01 to 2020-12-31. Those are every year Layer 2 later reported as out of sample. The survivors were chosen on the years their record was then quoted on, so the gate 1 verdict and the blind record are the same measurement twice.

contaminations.name: mode contamination -- two exits on at once
contaminations.touches_gate1: the FIRST sweep only; the three-mode rerun fixed it
contaminations.what: the original sweep ran the exit indicator and the baseline cross simultaneously with the C1-flip exit off, so every combination was testing "whichever of two exits fires first". Measured on the instrumented run the baseline cross took 44% of trend closes against the exit indicator's 7%. gate1_survivors_v1.csv is that run.

contaminations.name: field sight of 2016-2020
contaminations.what: W3 = 2016-2020 is inside the gate 1 score, so the candidate FIELD handed to every later stage was selected with sight of the years those stages treated as unseen. This is the same defect as #1 seen from the field's side rather than the score's.

contaminations.name: costs under-charged by atr_mult
contaminations.touches_gate1: NO at gate 1, YES everywhere downstream
contaminations.what: _cost_R returns the cost in RAW r units; when r is restated against a fixed 1.0xATR risk unit the cost has to be restated with it. Gate 1 runs every combination at atr_mult=1.0, so the factor is exactly 1.0 and the gate 1 numbers are unaffected -- but every tuned stage that moved the stop was under-charged, median 20%, p90 46%.

contaminations.name: vote timing (the Book look-ahead)
contaminations.what: gate 1 never nets. It aggregates per-combination R, so VOTE_ON_ENTRY_DAY has nothing to act on. The defect is real and fatal, but it enters at the Book, not here -- which is why the gate 1 survivor counts survived the vote-timing fix unchanged while every book number went negative.

contaminations.name: costs off entirely
contaminations.what: S.COSTS is None unless load_costs() is called. The gate 1 files on disk were produced before the costed path existed -- "Layer 2 charged NO costs at all before this: gates 1-3 to date are gross figures" (l2sweep.py). The honest gate 1 charges cost_table_h22 on every trade.
